teaser: The CFO hands you $2.4M and eight weeks: run discovery, sort hard SLAs from nice-to-haves, and get an architecture past the governance board.

scene.title: The CFO puts $2.4M on the table and gives you eight weeks to pass the governance board
scene.sceneHtml:
Board meeting, Week 1. The CFO presents a slide: "AI initiative budget: $2.4M over 12 months. Expected: measurable ROI across clinical operations, claims processing, and customer service. Your first task: run discovery workshops with each business unit and produce an architecture proposal that passes the governance review board."

You have eight weeks to surface requirements, evaluate architectures, and justify the investment. Here is what you must master.

takeaways: Functional = what the system does; non-functional = how well (p95 latency, accuracy, cost, compliance). A latency SLA is non-functional.
Five value pillars: Efficiency (throughput), Productivity (quality), Transformation (redeployment), Solution Cost, Performance SLA.
A stated SLA is a gate, not a trade-off: eliminate any option that violates it first, then compare survivors on cost and quality.
An ADR missing its alternatives and accepted trade-offs is incomplete; ask the author to add them before publishing, not later.
